summary: The circle here is drawn confidently in the wrong place three times, and each time the falsifying evidence was already inside the repo. (1) The four payload XMLs that GAUNTLET.md §1 uses to re-score the board and that lanes L1-L4 will port BYTE-EXACT are the ANDROID v0.682 files, byte-identical to reference/extracted/android/*.bin apart from the XML declaration; the web v0.717 payload carries none of those four roots (its 27 bindata files are 19 animdata + survivalmodedata + obj + name lists). The lane's own C2 correction says so; the standing engine does not. (2) The '.92/.96 frame-quantized cooldown' pattern is graded [CONTRACT] and BINDS future INFERRED values, but it is a derived display number: the web payload multiplies cooldown x 24 by a stat-driven modifier, the authored cooldowns are integers, and L0 banked an OVERTURN UPHELD x2 proving 4.96/9.92/8.92 are raw 5/10/9 at one reader's SPD. (3) src/config/chi.ts justifies inventing a Chi cost table with 'the study has NO frame-backed reads of skill Chi costs' - the Stage-2 kickoff it was implementing had said 'Chi Punch 10 dmg L1 / 2 Chi / 4.96 s CD' under a CONTRACT heading two days earlier, and the shipped cost is 30. Underneath all three is a mechanism gap: src/config/CLAUDE.md advertises the CONTRACT/INFERRED label invariant as 'test-enforced' and no test parses a label; the confidence tier is an honour system. Two further items: the artifact law (GAUNTLET §0) sets no precedence between a frame (A1) and a payload row (A2) while its only tiebreak - 'the frame wins' - inverts the precedence IMPROVEMENTS_RESEARCH.md:29 states; and GAUNTLET R1 rules on the copyright scope of three text categories from a grant document nobody in the workspace has ever read (reference/ still holds only its README, 31 days on).

findings.claim: GAUNTLET.md presents reference/extracted/{questdata,skilldata,npcdata,itemdata}.xml as the held payload that re-scores the board and sets BYTE-EXACT gates on them for four lanes (L1-L4), with no build label - but all four are the ANDROID v0.682 files, and the repo's own labelling rule forbids quoting v0.682 data as v0.717.
findings.cite: docs/GAUNTLET.md:73 (commit c2e5df9) and the L1-L4 byte-exact gates at :126,:128,:129,:130 (commit e97f91f); docs/research/fidelity/SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:124-127; docs/gauntlet/L0/SALVAGE.md:550-563

$ python3 difflib skilldata.xml vs android/117_Mobile_SkillData.bin

$ root element of every web bindata file (27 files): 19x <animdata>, 1x <survivalmodedata>, 1x <obj>, 6 plain name lists. No skill/item/quest/npc root anywhere in the web payload.

SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:124-127 -- "the four data tables in 3.7 come from the **android 0.682** build. They are tagged `CONTRACT-SRC (0.682)` and must never be quoted as 0.717."
GAUNTLET.md:73 -- "| `skilldata.xml` (40 K) | **75 skills x 182 level rows**, each with exact `<chi>`, `<cooldown>` ... |" (no build named anywhere in the table)
GAUNTLET.md:126 (L1 gate) -- "all 3,307 lines present byte-exact"; :128 (L2) -- "all 75 skills x 182 rows byte-exact from A2"; :129 (L3) -- "982 items byte-exact"; :130 (L4) -- "495 NPCs byte-exact"
SALVAGE.md:558-563 -- "So `reference/extracted/{questdata,skilldata,npcdata,itemdata}.xml` came from the **ANDROID** build ... Every row ported from those four files is **v0.682 until a WEB-side artifact says otherwise** - which raises build-parity risk for L1, L2, L3 and L4, the lanes that port them."
That the builds are differently tuned is already banked: docs/gauntlet/L0/wf-journal-wf3a2.jsonl -- "Android StatsManager.as:1856 `if(speed > 300)` and :1860 `return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5;` ... genuinely half the per-point effect" vs the web's cap 600.
findings.rule_targeted: GAUNTLET.md 0 (artifact A2) + 1 + 2 lane gates for L1-L4
findings.proposed_change: Two edits, both to GAUNTLET.md. (a) 0's artifact table, row A2 'What citing it looks like': 'file + the XML/AS3 line, quoted' -> 'file + BUILD (web 0.717 / android 0.682) + the XML/AS3 line, quoted'. (b) 1's table header cell 'Held, unmined, in `reference/extracted/`' -> 'Held, unmined, in `reference/extracted/` - all four are **android v0.682** (C2)'. Incident it would have prevented: SALVAGE.md:558's C2, which had to be re-derived first-hand mid-lane after a WF-2 critic had already claimed questdata had 'no parity hole'. Second-order consequence: every future A2 cite gets longer and some findings that read as CONTRACT-SRC will have to be re-graded as v0.682 - which is the point, but it will slow L1-L4 and it caps the achievable 1:1 on four of twelve systems, because the web build fetched those files over a dead network path and no web-side copy exists to check against. Rollback: revert the two cells; the C2 text in SALVAGE.md still records the risk.

findings.claim: The '.92/.96 frame-quantized cooldown' pattern is graded [CONTRACT] - the project's top confidence tier - and is bound as a rule for future INFERRED values, but it is a derived display number, not an authored one: the payload's own cooldowns are integers and the game multiplies them by a stat-driven modifier before display.
findings.evidence:
SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:573 -- "[CONTRACT] - Chi Punch cooldown is 4.96s (observed on-screen, A-02 t=7:05). All cooldowns follow a frame-quantized `.92/.96` ending pattern."
STAGE2_KICKOFF.md:73-74 -- "cooldowns are frame-quantized (.92/.96 endings); keep that pattern for any INFERRED cooldown values."
src/config/skills.ts ships that mandate: chiPunch 4960 /** CONTRACT */, smokeBomb 7960 /** INFERRED - .96 pattern */, stab 920 /** INFERRED - .92 pattern */.

The payload refutes it. $ distinct non-empty <cooldown> values in reference/extracted/skilldata.xml (98 of 182 rows):
['10','15','2','20','3','3.5','30','4','5','6','60','70','8','9']  -- not one ends in .92/.96.

Read first-hand in the decompiled web payload:
reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/(sect)1t105s0(sect).as:316-318 -- "_loc2_ = this.levelList[param1].cooldown * 24; ... return _loc2_ * (sect)1t1523s0(sect).(sect)1t9589s0(sect)();"
reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/(sect)1t1523s0(sect).as:2289-2295 -- "internal static function (sect)1t9590s0(sect)(param1:int) : Number { if(param1 > 600) param1 = 600; return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5; }"
i.e. displayed cooldown = authored seconds x 24 frames x (1 - SPD/1200). The .92/.96 endings are one player's stat, not the game's design.

L0 already banked the same conclusion, twice upheld:
docs/gauntlet/L0/wf-journal-run2.jsonl -- claim: "The ledger's 4.96 / 9.92 / 8.92 cooldowns are not contract values - they are one reader's SPD applied to the raw integers 5 / 10 / 9"; quote: "295: <cooldown>10</cooldown> / 302: <cooldown>9</cooldown>"; reproduction: "SPD 10: mod=0.991667  5s->4.96  10s->9.92  9s->8.92  <== matches ledger"
docs/gauntlet/L0/wf-journal-wf3a2.jsonl -- "HOLDS ON EVERY CLAUSE INCLUDING THE ARITHMETIC ... OVERTURN UPHELD" (two independent critics).
Nothing has propagated that back: :573 still reads [CONTRACT] and the kickoff still binds the pattern.
findings.rule_targeted: the CONTRACT/INFERRED confidence tier (src/config/CLAUDE.md invariant 1) + STAGE2_KICKOFF.md:73's standing instruction for INFERRED cooldowns
findings.proposed_change: Delete the second sentence of SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:573 ('All cooldowns follow a frame-quantized `.92/.96` ending pattern.', 8 words) and the clause at STAGE2_KICKOFF.md:73-74 ('cooldowns are frame-quantized (.92/.96 endings); keep that pattern for any INFERRED cooldown values.', 14 words). Incident it would have prevented: two INFERRED config values (smokeBomb 7960, stab 920) were manufactured to match an artifact of one player's SPD stat, and the [CONTRACT] grade has stood since 2026-07-17. Second-order consequence: skills.ts's chiPunch 4960 loses its stated basis and becomes an open L2 item rather than a settled number - correct, but it re-opens a value the duel prototype currently treats as fixed. Rollback: restore the two sentences. The config edit itself belongs to L2, not to this review (ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW 6 forbids moving src/).

findings.claim: src/config/chi.ts justifies inventing its entire Chi cost table with a stated ABSENCE of evidence that was false when written - the Stage-2 kickoff it was implementing already carried the measured Chi cost, under a CONTRACT heading, two days earlier - and the shipped value is 15x the measured one.
findings.evidence:
src/config/chi.ts:6-9 -- "ALL THREE are INFERRED tuning seeds - the study has NO frame-backed reads of skill Chi costs or an in-duel regen rate ... Revisit against real reads if later research surfaces costs." then CHI_COST = { chiPunch: 30, smokeBomb: 25, stab: 10 }.

The reads existed, in the repo, before that file:
SYNTHESIS.md:511 (committed 54ffb12, 2026-07-11) -- "| Chi Punch = 10 dmg L1 (confirmed) | exactly 10 dmg, 2 Chi, 4.96 s CD on-screen (A-02 t=7:05) | (check) double-confirmed + enriched (cost/CD) |"
SYNTHESIS.md:58 -- "| Chi Punch | 10 dmg | 20 dmg | 2 | 4.96 s (both) |" and the same table gives Focus 5 Chi and Dash 2 Chi.
STAGE2_KICKOFF.md:72 (committed ebc1335, 2026-07-11) -- "- **Skills (7, CONTRACT):** Chi Punch 10 dmg L1 / 2 Chi / 4.96 s CD"
$ git log --date=short -- src/config/chi.ts
47bab80 2026-07-13 Stage 3 M3: Chi meter + skill costs - Sim gate, B-23 HUD pair, chaos-proven (360/360)

The payload agrees with the small integers, not with 30: distinct non-empty <chi> values in skilldata.xml are ['0','10','100','2','20','3','5','50','6','7','8'].
And the file's own sibling contradicts CHI_MAX = 100: src/config/profile.ts:15 -- "/** CONTRACT (A-00) - fresh-profile pool maxes: HP / CHI / AP. */ export const PROFILE_START_POOLS = { hp: 10, chi: 10, ap: 30 };"
findings.rule_targeted: src/config/CLAUDE.md - 'Research verdicts for CONTRACT claims live in docs/research/original-game-facts.md - check there before correcting a value from memory' (there is no matching rule for claiming evidence is ABSENT)
findings.proposed_change: Add nine words to src/config/CLAUDE.md's Landmines: 'A docblock claiming NO evidence exists must cite the search that proves it.' Incident it would have prevented: chi.ts:6 asserted the study had no Chi-cost reads two days after the Stage-2 kickoff quoted one under a CONTRACT heading, and the false absence disarmed the file's own 'revisit if later research surfaces costs' escape hatch for 42 days. Second-order consequence: it makes 'we don't know X' more expensive to write than to leave unsaid, which risks silent gaps replacing stated ones - so pair it with 'unknown' being an acceptable label rather than a defect. Rollback: delete the sentence. The value fix (chiPunch 30 -> 2) is L2's, not this review's.

findings.claim: The gauntlet's LAW ranks nothing between a video frame (A1) and a payload row (A2), and its only tiebreak - 'the frame wins' - inverts the precedence the repo states everywhere else, so critics judging ~1,700 claims have been resolving frame-vs-payload collisions ad hoc.
findings.cite: docs/GAUNTLET.md:48-49 (artifact table A1/A2) and :59 (the tiebreak), commit c2e5df9; CLAUDE.md:15-16; docs/research/IMPROVEMENTS_RESEARCH.md:29-31; docs/research/fidelity/SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:19-23
findings.evidence:
GAUNTLET.md:59 -- "when a measurement doc and a frame disagree, **the frame wins** - say so out loud." (the A1..A5 table above it assigns no rank at all)
CLAUDE.md:15-16 -- "When a measurement doc and a frame disagree, **the frame wins** - say so."
IMPROVEMENTS_RESEARCH.md:29-31 -- "**Precedence (do not reorder):** decompiled source constants (CONTRACT-SRC) > measured OG behavior (`fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md` ...) > repo invariants (`CLAUDE.md`, folder rules) > anything in this document."
SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:19-23 -- "`CONTRACT-SRC` | read from the **Duels** payload's own code or data | **yes** - authoritative" / "`MEASURED` | from video frames | yes - **until a `CONTRACT-SRC` value replaces it**"
The collision is not hypothetical - CC-2 is exactly it: a correctly cited, correctly read frame (4.96 s on screen at A-02 t=7:05) produced a [CONTRACT] number the payload refutes. Critics are already improvising around it, e.g. docs/gauntlet/L0/wf-journal-s26a.jsonl -- "THE FRAME WINS - and here the frame is on the ledger's side. I confirmed the finding's datum ... But itemdata.xml is an ANDROID v0.682 artifact - per correction C2 the web payload..."
findings.rule_targeted: CLAUDE.md Invariants ('the frame wins') and GAUNTLET.md 0 (the artifact law)
findings.proposed_change: Scope the tiebreak in both places: '**the frame wins**' -> '**the frame wins on APPEARANCE; the payload wins on authored NUMBERS**' (+8 words each). Incident it would have prevented: SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:573's [CONTRACT] 4.96 s, a frame read of a number the payload authors as 5. Second-order consequence: it hands agents a second question ('is this claim about appearance or about a number?') that some claims straddle - a slash's reach is both - so expect a small class of arguments about which half a claim falls in; the honest default is that anything with a unit is a number. Rollback: restore the two lines; the rule's original incident (SESSION 18's A4-D, a bare doll graded as clothed) is an appearance case and is unaffected either way.

findings.claim: The label invariant that carries this project's entire epistemics is advertised as test-enforced and no test enforces it - nothing in the suite parses a CONTRACT/INFERRED label.
findings.evidence:
src/config/CLAUDE.md:6-9 -- "## Invariants (test-enforced - `tests/config-purity.test.ts` + `tests/config-values.test.ts`)\n- Every value is labeled **CONTRACT** ... **INFERRED** ... or **Spec-fixed** ... Keep the label honest when you touch a value."
$ grep -n 'describe(\|it(' tests/config-purity.test.ts
50: describe('config-purity: src/core/')  51: it('contains ZERO numeric literals')  58: it('imports only from src/core/ or src/config/')  62: it('contains no unscannable payload files')  67: describe('config-purity: src/config/')  68: it('imports only from within src/config/')  72: it('contains no unscannable payload files')  77: describe('scanner self-test')  110/147/153: scanner regression tests
-- no label test. In tests/config-values.test.ts labels appear only inside comments, e.g. ':574  chiPunch: 4960, // CONTRACT (A-02 on-screen)'.
$ grep -rn 'scanLabelCoverage' . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git
docs/research/IMPROVEMENTS_RESEARCH.md:1633 -- "Add a `scanLabelCoverage()` to tests/utils/configPurity.ts + a describe block in config-purity.test.ts" (still an open proposal, so the gap is known)
The taxonomy has also drifted past the three names the file lists: CONTRACT-SRC, 'CONTRACT (research)', 'CONTRACT (frame-backed)' and 'INFERRED-from-measurement' are all in use (src/config/stats.ts:63,66; economy.ts:45; xp.ts:22).
findings.proposed_change: Cheapest honest fix is a deletion: strike 'test-enforced - ' from src/config/CLAUDE.md:6 (-2 words) so the header stops claiming a gate that does not exist, and let the standing 'if you check it by eye twice, build the gate' rule schedule scanLabelCoverage(). Incident it would have prevented: CC-2 and CC-3 are both label failures that a label gate would not have caught either (it checks presence, not honesty) - which is the honest limit of this finding and the reason the deletion beats the test as the first move. Second-order consequence: removing the words admits the invariant is an honour system, which may reduce trust in existing labels - correct, and preferable to false assurance. Rollback: restore the two words, or land scanLabelCoverage() and keep them.

findings.claim: A folder CLAUDE.md - loaded as a binding rule on every session - still states the palette policy the owner reversed 31 days ago, and points at root CLAUDE.md as its authority for a line root CLAUDE.md explicitly retired.
findings.cite: src/config/CLAUDE.md:14-16 (last touched e8a6d82, 2026-07-12); docs/MASTER_SPEC.md (28e7d0b, 2026-07-24); CLAUDE.md:18-22; src/config/palette.ts:4-9
findings.evidence:
$ git log --date=short -- src/config/CLAUDE.md
e8a6d82 2026-07-12 Palette: revert trade-dress shift to near-OG hues (owner veto 2026-07-12)
15a7f08 2026-07-11 Stage 0: scaffold
(i.e. nothing since 2026-07-12)
src/config/CLAUDE.md:14-16 -- "- `palette.ts` sits at near-OG hues (owner veto of the trade-dress shift, 2026-07-12). Drawings stay original - the palette is the only thing that moved toward the original."
docs/MASTER_SPEC.md -- "**Supersedes** the 'RECREATE, NEVER RIP' art restriction as previously scoped, the palette policy (2026-07-12) ..." and "**Palette**: exact OG values allowed (the near-OG policy is superseded)."
CLAUDE.md:18-19 -- "**LICENSED 1:1 RECREATION (owner ruling 2026-07-24 - supersedes the old 'never traced/transcribed' art line and the 2026-07-12 palette policy).**"
src/config/palette.ts:8-9 compounds it -- "the DRAWINGS remain original work (that line still holds - see root CLAUDE.md)" - a pointer to the document that retired that exact line.
findings.proposed_change: Delete src/config/CLAUDE.md:14-16 outright (-29 words). Root CLAUDE.md already carries the live ruling and docs/MASTER_SPEC.md carries the detail, so the bullet adds nothing but a contradiction. Incident it would have prevented: no measured incident - this is a latent one, and I am saying so rather than inventing a cite; the observable damage today is that palette.ts:8 cites root CLAUDE.md as authority for a superseded line. Second-order consequence: src/config/ loses its local reminder that palette values are double-entered in tests/config-values.test.ts - so keep the separate double-entry bullet at :17-19, which is untouched by the ruling. Rollback: restore the three lines.

findings.claim: GAUNTLET R1 rules on the copyright scope of three categories of Lut's text from a grant document that nobody in this workspace has ever read, and the five-minute evidence step that would let anyone read it has been open for 31 days.
findings.cite: docs/GAUNTLET.md:314-332 (R1, commit e97f91f); docs/MASTER_SPEC.md ('Status: recorded in the project notes' + 'Scope caution until the grant's exact wording is checked'); ls reference/
findings.evidence:
GAUNTLET.md:323-332 (R1) -- "**Scope, since 'dialogue' has four meanings in this payload** - the owner confirmed the first; the rest are **decided here on the identical rights logic** (all Lut's text, private repo, development use)" then marks Quest + step titles '(check) decided', UI copy '(check) decided', Item + skill names/descriptions 'same policy once the string table is found'.
docs/MASTER_SPEC.md -- "Status: **recorded in the project notes**" and "**Scope caution until the grant's exact wording is checked**: assume personal / non-commercial recreation. Before ANY distribution or monetization, re-read the PM/email wording (and ideally confirm scope with Lut in one message: distribution? credit line? commercial?)."
$ ls -la reference/
total 8
drwxr-xr-x  3 kheshav staff  96 Jul 24 00:25 .
-rw-r--r--  1 kheshav staff 270 Jul 24 00:25 README.md
-- only the placeholder README ('Drop the Lut Games evidence here'), 31 days after the ruling.
The scope this rides on is not small: GAUNTLET.md:75 -- "**61 quests / 2,771 `<dialogue>` blocks / 3,307 verbatim `<text>` lines / 471 `<choice>`**", all queued for commit into src/ by L1.
findings.rule_targeted: GAUNTLET.md 6 R1 (the verbatim-text ruling) and CLAUDE.md's LICENSED 1:1 RECREATION invariant
findings.proposed_change: In R1's scope table, replace the two '(check) decided' cells and the 'same policy once the string table is found' cell with 'UNRULED until the grant's wording is read' (-25 words removed, +21 added, net -4), leaving the one owner-confirmed row as the only green light and keeping R1's existing public/ship-build gate. Incident it would have prevented: the ruling document's own five-minute evidence TODO has been open since 2026-07-24 and R1 decided three more categories without it - a decision an agent cannot make, because the document being interpreted is not in the workspace. Second-order consequence: L1 can still port character dialogue (the owner-confirmed row) so the lane is not blocked, but quest titles and UI copy would need paraphrase or a hold, which costs 1:1 on those surfaces until the owner archives the PM - exactly the trade R1's own veto note describes. Rollback: restore the three cells.
